newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on commercial/commission buying.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on commercial/commission buying.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on commercial, commission house and fund buying, traders said.

"There was early fund short covering of about 500 to 700 January-buying from elevator companies, then commercials and commission houses bought when soybeans and meal came back," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $0.10. January futures crush profit margin rose to -37.73 from -35.60 on Thursday. Volume was 3,820 lots, 76,400 tonnes, with 140 hedge lots.
January canola rose $1.40 to close at $401.40 and March rose $1.10 to $401.60. March flax climbed $0.60 to $350.60 on commercial demand. Jan-Mar spread at $4, UGG sold 85 Mar-May at $3.
February western barley lost $0.20 to $134.40 with LFG buying at the close, May fell $0.50 to $133.60. Volume was 650 lots. Feb-May spread at $0.70. Oats did not trade.

March feed wheat lost $0.10 to $167.90 on commission selling and UGG buying at the close, traders said. Volume was 80 lots. Sparks Cos' U.S. corn production estimate, reported by the trade at 9.29 billion bushels, was somewhat bearish to the WCE feed grain complex, WCE traders said.
Sparks officials were unavailable for comment on the estimate.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
